title_en: Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Comprehensively Strengthening Judicial Protection of Minors and Crime Prevention and Control Work
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Opinion on Comprehensively Strengthening Judicial Protection and Crime Prevention for Minors

Fa Fa [2024] No. 7

Children and minors are the future of the motherland and the hope of the nation. In the new era and new journey, society as a whole is more concerned with the comprehensive and healthy growth of children and minors, and has put forward new and higher requirements for the protection of minors' rights and interests and crime prevention. The people's courts bear heavier responsibilities and face greater challenges. To comprehensively strengthen the judicial protection of minors and the prevention and control of crimes, and to effectively enhance the level of protection of minors' rights and interests, this Opinion is formulated in accordance with the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Minors, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Prevention of Juvenile Delinquency, and other relevant laws and regulations, based on the actual work of the people's courts.

I. General Requirements

1. Guiding Ideology. Adhere to the guidance of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, thoroughly implement Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law, earnestly study and implement General Secretary Xi Jinping's important expositions on the work concerning children and minors, and plan and promote the judicial protection of minors and the prevention and control of crimes from the political height of comprehensively advancing the construction of a strong country and the great cause of national rejuvenation through Chinese-style modernization. Firmly establish the concept of judicial protection of minors in the new era, practice the core socialist values, promote the spirit of socialist rule of law, and promote the integrated development of the "six major protections" of family protection, school protection, social protection, network protection, government protection, and judicial protection through law-based and proactive performance of duties, so as to create a good legal and social environment for the comprehensive and healthy growth of minors.

2. Basic Principles

(1) Adhere to the principle of the best interests of the child. Always place the protection of minors' rights and interests and their development needs first in the judicial protection of minors, respect the dignity of minors, combine the growth and physical and mental characteristics of minors, legally protect the reputation, privacy, and various substantive rights and litigation rights of minors involved in cases, implement the concept of "special, priority, mutual, and comprehensive" protection in all stages and links, and fully safeguard and guarantee the legitimate rights and interests of minors.

(2) Adhere to the principle of integrated and integrated performance of duties. Deepen the reform of comprehensive adjudication of "three trials in one" in criminal, civil, and administrative cases, strengthen systematic thinking, adhere to comprehensive protection, and at the same time pay attention to the maintenance of civil and administrative rights and interests of minors involved, the prevention and punishment of criminal offenses, and the protection of public interests. Highlight problem orientation, improve the working mechanism, work together with all parties, substantively resolve prominent issues that infringe upon the legitimate rights and interests of minors, promote the transformation from post-hoc relief protection to in-process and pre-hoc prevention and governance, and build a full-chain, all-round, three-dimensional protection network for minors.

(3) Adhere to the principle of equal emphasis on case handling and promoting governance. Handle cases involving minors fairly and efficiently in accordance with the law, ensuring the organic unity of political effect, social effect, and legal effect in case handling. While handling cases, deeply analyze the deep-seated problems reflected in the cases in terms of family protection, school protection, social protection, network protection, government protection, etc., and promote the integration and synergy of the "six major protections" through more effective judicial protection, adhere to both punishment and prevention, address both symptoms and root causes, and implement source governance and systematic governance.

(4) Adhere to the principle of upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground. In response to the new circumstances and new situations in the judicial protection of minors, deeply summarize the legal rules concerning minors, combine with local actual conditions, and actively explore new mechanisms and methods conducive to strengthening the protection of minors' rights and interests and crime prevention. Adhere to the combination of top-level design and grassroots initiative, comprehensively promote theoretical innovation, institutional innovation, and practical innovation in judicial protection of minors, and continuously transform the institutional advantages of socialist juvenile justice with Chinese characteristics into comprehensive effectiveness in the protection of minors.

II. Strengthening Trial Work for Cases Involving Minors

(1) Strengthening Civil and Administrative Trial Work Involving Minors

3. Enhance the concept of protection of minors and crime prevention. Focus on the protection of minors and crime prevention, actively explore trial methods suitable for the physical and mental characteristics of minors, pay attention to the physical and mental health of minors in civil and administrative trials, be good at discovering emerging and tendentious problems, timely resolve and eliminate various negative factors that may breed illegal and criminal behaviors of minors, and effectively implement "grasping the front end and treating diseases before they occur."

4. Establish a fast-track handling mechanism for cases involving minors. Open a "green channel," based on the principles of convenience and efficiency, for civil and administrative cases involving the protection of minors' rights and interests, achieve priority case filing, rapid trial, timely judgment, and efficient enforcement, and effectively protect the legitimate rights and interests of minors.

5. Strengthen education and litigation guidance. Centering on protecting the comprehensive and healthy growth of minors, pay attention to providing targeted education and litigation guidance to minors, guardians, and other relevant persons from the aspects of legal provisions, social morality, and the laws of minors' physical and mental development during case handling. In divorce and other cases involving minor children, effectively implement the "Caring for Minors Tips" work, guide the parties to properly handle matters related to custody, visitation, property, etc., with the aim of ensuring the healthy growth of minor children.

6. Substantively refine mediation work. For civil cases, except for those not suitable for mediation such as confirmation of kinship, mediation should be emphasized. With the consent of both parties, social observers, close relatives of the minor, schools, sub-districts, neighborhood committees, village committees, etc., may be invited to participate in case mediation. For administrative cases, pre-litigation mediation should be actively carried out. For cases involving administrative compensation, damages, and the exercise of discretionary power by administrative agencies as provided by laws and regulations, attention should be paid during the trial to achieving the best case effect through mediation.

7. Timely appoint agents in litigation. In civil litigation, if there is a conflict of interest between a minor and his or her guardian, the people's court may promptly inform other persons legally qualified to be guardians to negotiate and determine the minor's agent; if negotiation fails, the people's court shall appoint an agent from among them. If the minor has no other person legally qualified to be a guardian, the people's court may appoint the relevant organization stipulated in Article 32 of the Civil Code as the agent.

8. Reasonably determine the person with direct custody. For custody cases, if the minor child has reached the age of eight, his or her opinions shall be fully heard and his or her true wishes shall be respected. When a minor child expresses wishes or states facts to the people's court, the people's court may notify social observers or other suitable persons to be present. The accompanying persons may assist the minor child in expressing his or her true wishes. When necessary, the people's court may separately question and hear the opinions of the minor child and provide a friendly environment suitable for the minor's psychological characteristics, ensuring his or her privacy and safety. If the minor child's expressed opinions are detrimental to his or her healthy physical and mental development, the people's court shall explain this and adjudicate in accordance with the principle of the best interests of the child.

9. Properly hear visitation rights cases. For visitation rights cases, the people's court shall, in the judgment document, specify the specific content such as visitation time and method based on the actual circumstances of the case. If the parent without direct custody cannot visit in person due to reasons such as working away from home, the people's court may guide the parties to actively provide parental affection to the child through telephone, letters, internet, video calls, etc.

The parent who does not directly raise the minor child shall exercise visitation rights at the time and in the manner agreed upon by the agreement, determined in the people's court judgment or mediation, without affecting the minor child's study and life. The parent with direct custody shall cooperate. If the parent with direct custody refuses to cooperate, the people's court may impose education, reprimand, or even take coercive measures such as detention or fines in accordance with the law. If visitation is detrimental to the minor child's physical and mental health and a party requests suspension of visitation, the people's court, after consulting the opinions of both parties and the minor child and verifying the facts, if it deems that visitation needs to be suspended, shall issue a ruling in accordance with the law. If a minor child requests visitation from parents, or grandparents request visitation from grandchildren, the people's court shall adjudicate in accordance with the law based on the specific circumstances of the case and the principle of the best interests of the child.

10. Properly hear tort cases involving minors. If a minor causes harm to another person, the guardian shall bear tort liability. If the guardian has fulfilled his or her guardianship duties, the tort liability may be mitigated. If the people's court finds that the guardian has not correctly performed his or her guardianship duties, it may reprimand the guardian and order him or her to receive education and guidance.

If a minor's personal rights are infringed upon, the people's court shall fully consider the minor's needs for development, growth, and recovery, and determine the compensation amount in accordance with the law. Necessary rehabilitation expenses for necessary functional recovery training determined according to medical certificates or appraisal conclusions, appropriate plastic surgery expenses, and other follow-up treatment expenses may be compensated together with the medical expenses already incurred. When determining the amount of moral damages, the amount may be appropriately increased compared to adult cases based on the specific circumstances of the case.

11. Legally protect the legitimate property rights and interests of minors. When trying divorce cases, the people's court shall pay attention to examining whether the property to be divided by the parties includes the property of the minor child and whether the property of the minor child has been separated, to prevent the parties from illegally disposing of the minor child's property. If the minor child has special circumstances such as serious illness, the people's court shall, based on the specific circumstances of the property, handle the matter in accordance with the principle of taking care of the rights and interests of the child, the wife/husband, and the innocent party. When trying inheritance cases, the people's court shall legally protect the minor's right of inheritance and right to bequeath.

12. Strengthen the legality review of administrative actions. For administrative actions involving the rights and interests of minors, the people's court shall strictly conduct a legality review to prevent administrative actions from infringing upon the rights and interests of minors. For illegal or improper administrative actions, correct them in a timely manner. Supervise and support education, public security, civil affairs, cyberspace administration, and other relevant departments in legally performing their statutory duties to protect the legitimate rights and interests of minors.

13. Strengthen the review of administrative permits and penalties. In cases involving administrative permits and administrative penalties concerning minors, pay attention to the special circumstances and rights protection needs of minors. For administrative permits in the fields of education and health, ensure that the minor's right to education and right to health are fully guaranteed; for administrative penalties involving minors, fully consider the minor's cognitive ability and behavioral characteristics to avoid improper penalties.

14. Strengthen governance of administrative disputes at the source. For matters such as the introduction of major reform measures, formulation or adjustment of policies, and handling of sensitive incidents that affect the vital interests of minors, the people's court may, through methods such as participating in argumentation, providing legal advisory opinions, and sending judicial recommendations, promote the scientific, democratic, and legal formulation of major administrative decisions concerning minors, effectively strengthen the protection of minors' rights and interests, and reduce and eliminate administrative actions infringing upon minors' rights and interests from the source.

15. Actively explore and innovate enforcement work mechanisms. Explore the assignment of dedicated teams or personnel to handle the enforcement of civil and administrative cases involving minors. For enforcement cases involving custody, visitation, etc., actively carry out education, guidance, and mediation work, guide the parties to voluntarily perform obligations or reach a settlement based on the principle of favoring the healthy physical and mental development of the minor child.

(2) Strengthening Criminal Trial Work Involving Minors

16. Tolerate but not condone juvenile delinquency. Precisely implement the criminal policy of combining leniency and severity, legally implement the policy of "education, reform, and rescue," adhere to the principle of "education as the mainstay, punishment as a supplement," accurately grasp and judge the social harmfulness of criminal acts, fully consider the minor's growth experience and the deep-seated reasons leading to the crime, and maximize the rescue of the minors involved. For those with deep subjective malice, heinous circumstances, serious harm, especially those who refuse to mend their ways despite repeated education, never tolerate or condone, resolutely punish in accordance with the law, and ensure judicial justice.

When trying cases of juvenile delinquency, adopt trial methods suitable for the physical and mental characteristics of minors, adhere to "integrating education into trial," conduct targeted court education based on the actual situation of the minor defendant's personality traits and criminal behavior, analyze the subjective and objective causes and lessons that led to the crime, guide the minor defendant to correctly understand the seriousness of the court trial and the social harmfulness of the criminal behavior, and promote his/her reform and renewal.

17. Severely punish the use of minors to commit illegal and criminal acts. For luring, instructing, or using minors to carry out illegal and criminal activities, if it constitutes a crime, impose a heavier punishment in accordance with the law. In particular, for crimes that seriously damage the physical and mental health of minors and seriously endanger social harmony and stability, such as coercing, instigating, luring, or deceiving minors to participate in the commission of crimes by mafia-like organizations or organized illegal activities; using minors to introduce or lure other younger minor females into prostitution or for rape; using minors who have not reached the age of criminal responsibility, left-behind children, or school students to commit crimes; and teaching minors criminal methods, providing drugs, controlled narcotic or psychotropic substances, or instilling obscene, violent, or other harmful information into minors and then using them, shall be severely punished in accordance with the law.

18. Severely punish crimes against minors. For crimes such as kidnapping, abducting, or trafficking children; violent injury, sexual assault of minors; luring, introducing, organizing, or forcing minors into prostitution; producing, selling, or disseminating obscene electronic information containing content involving minors; and disseminating obscene materials to minors, which seriously infringe upon the physical and mental health of minors, adhere to a zero-tolerance stance and severely punish in accordance with the law.

19. Strengthen the protection of the rights of minor victims. When trying criminal cases of infringement against minors, the people's court shall fully consider the characteristics of minor victims, whose physical and mental development is not yet mature and who are vulnerable to harm, provide special and priority protection, and strengthen the protection of their rights and interests. Promptly inform minor victims and their legal representatives of the case progress and case handling results, and provide explanations of the relevant circumstances. After determining the trial date, inform minor victims and their legal representatives of the time and place of the trial. After the judgment is pronounced, serve the judgment on the minor victims and their legal representatives.

(3) Deepening and Substantively Conducting Characteristic Trial Work Involving Minors

20. Deepen the protection of minors' privacy. For criminal cases where the defendant is under eighteen years of age at the time of trial, never conduct public trials; for civil and administrative cases involving minors and involving personal privacy, public trials shall not be conducted. For criminal cases involving minors, the names, addresses, photographs, and other information that may identify the minor's identity shall not be disclosed to the outside world. Case materials that are consulted, extracted, or copied and involve minors shall not be disclosed or disseminated. For civil and administrative cases involving minors, care shall be taken to protect the privacy of minors. When publishing cases or producing legal publicity materials, necessary technical processing of relevant information shall be carried out.

21. Thoroughly conduct social investigations. When trying cases of juvenile delinquency, the people's court shall understand in detail the minor's growth environment and the causes of the crime. For social investigation reports submitted by the people's procuratorate and written materials submitted by relevant personnel reflecting the situation of the minor defendant, the people's court shall focus on examining whether they objectively and comprehensively reflect the minor's personality traits, family guardianship situation, school education, social contacts, growth experience, performance before and after committing the crime, and other content that reflects the deep-seated reasons for the minor's path to crime. If the social investigation report is not specific or detailed, the people's court shall notify the people's procuratorate to supplement it, or may conduct a social investigation on its own or entrust relevant institutions to do so. Social investigation reports and relevant materials submitted by relevant personnel, after being presented, cross-examined, and legally adopted, may be used as references for handling the case and educating the defendant, and as a basis for making judicial recommendations to relevant parties. During the trial, the people's court may notify the person who made the investigation report to appear in court to explain the situation and accept questions from the prosecution, the defense, and the court.

22. Actively improve social observation. When the people's court tries civil cases involving minors such as divorce, custody, adoption, guardianship, and visitation, it may entrust social organizations or personnel engaged in the protection of minors to conduct investigations into the minor's relevant circumstances, participate in case mediation, accompany the minor to receive questioning when necessary, provide psychological counseling to the minor, and carry out post-judgment extension observation and protection as social observation work. Social observers may gain a comprehensive understanding of the minor's actual living conditions by listening to the opinions of the parties and the minor separately and visiting sub-districts, communities, kindergartens, schools, etc. The social observation report may serve as a reference and basis for the people's court in trying the case and conducting judicial extension work.

23. Actively provide psychological counseling. When trying cases involving minors, if deemed necessary based on the circumstances of the case, the people's court may provide psychological counseling and treatment to the minor parties on its own or by hiring professionals, to soothe the minor's emotions, eliminate or resolve the minor's psychological crisis and psychological disorders; with the consent of the minor and his/her legal representative, psychological assessment may also be conducted on the minor, and the psychological assessment report may serve as a reference for handling the case and educating and rehabilitating the minor. Promptly provide psychological counseling to minor victims and minors who have experienced domestic violence.

24. Increase relief efforts. Based on the actual difficulties of minors, provide priority relief to minors who meet the conditions for judicial relief, and provide preferential treatment in the intensity of relief. Actively establish a joint care and relief connection mechanism with education, civil affairs, the Communist Youth League, the Women's Federation, other departments, and social charitable institutions, and provide financial assistance, school transfer placement, and other assistance to minors in need to the greatest extent to protect the legitimate rights and interests of minors.

III. Promoting the Substantive Integration of Criminal, Civil, and Administrative "Three Trials in One" Involving Minors

25. Improve the integrated trial mechanism. For cases involving criminal, civil, and administrative cross-issues involving minors arising from the same facts or related facts, in principle, they shall be tried by the same trial organization, provided that it complies with the relevant jurisdictional provisions of the law and conditions permit. If prominent issues or hidden dangers in the administration of minors or crime prevention reflected in civil cases involving minors are found, or if during the trial of criminal cases involving minors, it is discovered that the minor's civil rights have also been infringed upon, they shall be properly resolved and handled together in accordance with the law. The basic facts confirmed by effective criminal or administrative judgments, unless there is contrary evidence sufficient to overturn them, may be recognized in related civil cases.

26. Properly handle the transfer of leads and the notification of rights. When trying cases such as disputes over modification of custody relationships, visitation rights disputes, and revocation of guardianship qualifications, and it is found that a minor is or is suspected of being subjected to illegal or criminal infringement such as abuse, violent injury, sexual assault, or abandonment, the leads suspected of illegal or criminal activities shall be transferred to the competent authorities for handling. When trying administrative cases and it is found that a minor's civil legitimate rights and interests have been infringed upon, the parties may be informed to file a separate civil lawsuit. If illegal or criminal activities are suspected, the leads shall be transferred to the competent authorities for handling. When trying criminal cases involving minors and it is found that the minor's parents or other guardians fail to lawfully perform guardianship duties or infringe upon the minor's legitimate rights and interests, and illegal or criminal activities are suspected, or other leads of crimes infringing upon minors' rights and interests are discovered, the leads shall be transferred to the competent authorities for handling.

27. Ensure proper coordination between criminal and civil proceedings. For cases where a minor commits a crime but is not subject to criminal liability due to not reaching the age of criminal responsibility, or cases of sexual assault against minors where criminal liability cannot be pursued due to objective reasons such as the statute of limitations for criminal prosecution having expired, but which meet the statute of limitations for the right to claim damages under Article 191 of the Civil Code of the PRC, or other cases involving infringement of minors' rights that do not yet constitute a crime, if the parties initiate civil litigation, the people's court shall support such actions in accordance with the law, and the scope of compensation shall be determined in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Civil Code of the PRC. Where minors suffer sexual assault or other injuries in venues such as hotels, inns, karaoke bars, bars, internet cafes, e-sports hotels, script entertainment establishments, or on internet platforms, and the relevant venues or platforms fail to fulfill their safety and security obligations, if the minor initiates civil litigation on this ground, the people's court shall support such actions in accordance with the law, and the scope of compensation shall be determined in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Civil Code of the PRC. Where evidence relevant to the alleged infringing act is preserved by public security organs, procuratorial organs, or the people's court, and the parties to the infringement case or their agents ad litem are unable to collect it themselves due to objective reasons, and they apply for the court to investigate and collect it, the people's court shall grant the application, except where it may affect ongoing criminal proceedings.

28. Establish a衔接 mechanism for public interest litigation. Where a people's court discovers that the lawful rights and interests of a minor have been infringed upon and the matter involves the public interest, it may transfer the leads to the procuratorial organ. Attention shall be paid to discovering whether food, toys, supplies, etc., involving minors in the case, endanger the physical and mental health of an unspecified number of minors; a comprehensive review shall be conducted of whether internet technologies, products, and services involved in the case, such as online games, live streaming, audio and video, social networking, and websites, as well as books, radio and television, film and television media, etc., contain information harmful to the physical and mental health of minors; and whether administrative organs with supervisory and management duties for the protection of minors have engaged in omissions, misconduct, or other circumstances that harm the public interests of minors.

IV. Promote the Integrated Force of the "Six Protections"

29. Guide guardians to fulfill their guardianship duties in accordance with the law. People's courts shall, during trials, strengthen the guardianship responsibilities of parents and other guardians, guide guardians to fulfill their obligations of upbringing, education, and protection, create a family environment conducive to the healthy growth of minors, and not only provide guarantees for the health and safety of minors but also pay attention to their psychological conditions and emotional needs. Properly adjudicate cases of applying for the determination and designation of guardians to ensure that minors have guardians; properly adjudicate cases of applying for the change of guardian and revocation of guardianship qualification to ensure that minors receive appropriate guardianship; where a guardian fails to perform guardianship duties or infringes on the lawful rights and interests of the ward, order the guardian to bear corresponding legal liability in accordance with the law.

30. Strengthen family education guidance. Where a people's court adjudicates cases involving special groups such as left-behind minors and minors in distress, or civil cases involving minors such as divorce, custody, adoption, guardianship, visitation, etc., it shall, based on the specific circumstances of the case, at various stages including pre-litigation mediation, case trial, and post-judgment follow-up, carry out family education guidance through various forms such as court education, legal interpretation and reasoning, on-site counseling, online counseling, psychological intervention, issuance of a family education responsibility notification, and a family education guidance proposal. Where, in the trial of criminal or administrative cases involving minors, a people's court finds that the parents or other guardians of a minor do not perform their guardianship duties in accordance with the law, infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of the minor, or there are other circumstances due to omission or improper family supervision and education that may affect the physical and mental health of the minor, the court shall, depending on the circumstances, admonish the parents or other guardians of the minor and may order them to accept family education guidance.

31. Strictly handle student bullying in accordance with the law. Where a people's court discovers the existence of student bullying in relevant cases, it shall communicate with the school or training institution and the competent education department, recommend that it be dealt with seriously and promptly, and follow up on the progress of the handling. Where a minor suffers harm due to student bullying or other conduct, the people's court shall comprehensively consider various factors such as the intensity and duration of the bullying conduct and the resulting damage to the victim's physical and psychological well-being, and shall adjudicate the tortfeasor to bear tort liability in accordance with the law. Give full play to the functions and roles of apology in repair, consolation, and deterrence, and explore the use of pre-litigation mediation and other means to encourage minors who have engaged in student bullying to sincerely apologize. Where schools, training institutions, etc., fail to fulfill their education and management duties, they shall be adjudicated to bear tort liability in accordance with the law, and a judicial suggestion shall be issued depending on the circumstances. Where the bullying conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.

32. Properly handle campus disputes. When adjudicating campus dispute cases, people's courts shall, on the basis of ascertaining the facts and clarifying responsibilities, properly resolve disputes in accordance with the law. Actively guide the parties to assert their rights lawfully and rationally, and resolutely punish various illegal and criminal acts such as "campus disturbances" in accordance with the law, to maintain the normal order of education and teaching in schools. Where a minor suffers personal injury during the period of study and life at school, and the school has fulfilled its education and management duties, the school shall be adjudicated not to bear tort liability in accordance with the law, providing judicial guarantee for schools to carry out teaching management in accordance with laws and regulations.

33. Strengthen the construction of the team of vice principals for rule of law. Actively select business backbone with strong political quality, solid legal knowledge, rich practical experience, and expertise in publicity and education to serve as vice principals for rule of law, clarify work responsibilities, strictly enforce work requirements, and further establish and improve long-term communication mechanisms and normalized information feedback mechanisms with education administrative departments and schools, to enhance the effectiveness of the performance of duties by vice principals for rule of law.

34. Timely propose recommendations for specialized education. Where a people's court, in adjudicating cases involving minors, discovers that a minor has engaged in conduct stipulated in Article 44 of the Law of the PRC on the Prevention of Juvenile Delinquency and requires specialized education, it may make recommendations to the relevant departments.

35. Establish a mechanism for analyzing and reporting the causes of crime on a case-by-case basis. For each case of juvenile delinquency, conduct an in-depth analysis of whether there are circumstances such as weak or inadequate protections from family, schools, society, the internet, government, and judicial protection behind the case, and form a report to be attached to the case file, with separate explanations provided during case evaluation. Where it is discovered that relevant entities have failed to fulfill their protection duties such as education, management, rescue, and care for minors, the people's court shall promptly send a judicial suggestion to the relevant entity; where suspected illegal or criminal conduct is involved, promptly transfer the relevant leads to the competent department for handling.

36. Establish a mechanism for analyzing and reporting on the implementation of the mandatory reporting system. For cases where a minor has been harmed, conduct a case-by-case review of whether relevant state organs, residents' committees, villagers' committees, entities and personnel in close contact with minors, when discovering in their work that a minor's physical or mental health has been harmed, is suspected of being harmed, or faces other dangerous situations, have fulfilled the mandatory reporting obligation, and form a report to be attached to the case file, with separate explanations provided during case evaluation. Where circumstances exist where reporting should have been made but was not, a judicial suggestion shall be promptly sent; where suspected disciplinary violations or illegal or criminal conduct is involved, promptly transfer the relevant leads to the competent department for handling.

37. Establish a mechanism for analyzing and reporting on the implementation of statutory obligations at relevant venues. For cases involving minors that occur in venues such as hotels, inns, and e-sports hotels, review whether, when accommodating minors for check-in, the operator has fulfilled the obligation to inquire about the minor's age, the contact information of their parents or other guardians, the identity relationship with the co-occupant, etc., whether the relevant venue has set up relevant signs, etc., and form a report to be attached to the case file, with separate explanations provided during case evaluation. Where problems are discovered, a judicial suggestion shall be promptly sent; where suspected illegal or criminal conduct is involved, promptly transfer the relevant leads to the competent department for handling.

38. Establish a special analysis and reporting mechanism for network protection. For cases involving minors that relate to the internet, based on the causes of the case and the provisions of the laws on the protection of minors, establish a collaborative mechanism with relevant functional departments to review whether the relevant subjects have fulfilled their statutory obligations for the protection of minors online, and form a report to be attached to the case file, with separate explanations provided during case evaluation. Where problems are discovered, a judicial suggestion shall be promptly sent to the relevant internet enterprise or competent department; where suspected illegal or criminal conduct is involved, promptly transfer the relevant leads to the competent department for handling.

39. Enhance the systematic nature and targeted approach of legal publicity and education. Strengthen communication and collaboration with schools and education administrative departments, actively carry out legal publicity and education suited to the characteristics of minors, adhere to combining seriousness with acceptability, knowledge with interest, and universality with particularity, strengthen the use of cases to explain the law, innovate forms of publicity, educate and guide minors to abide by the law and discipline, continuously enhance their awareness of rules, rule of law, and responsibility, and effectively strengthen their awareness and ability of self-protection.

All higher people's courts shall strengthen the review, supervision, and guidance of the release of typical criminal cases involving minors by courts within their jurisdiction to ensure good social results.

V. Strengthen Organizational Guarantees

40. Strengthen professional capacity building. Strictly implement the provisions of the Law on the Protection of Minors and other legal provisions, designate specialized institutions or designate specialized personnel to adjudicate cases involving minors and be responsible for the prevention and control of juvenile crime, and strengthen the construction of trial teams for the "three-in-one trial" (civil, criminal, administrative). Enrich the work force for juvenile trial, and integratively advance the construction of the team's political quality, professional quality, and professional ethics quality. Personnel adjudicating cases involving minors shall undergo specialized training, be familiar with the physical and psychological characteristics of minors, and be passionate about the protection of minors. Strengthen the allocation of full-time auxiliary personnel to assist trial personnel in carrying out extended protection work for minors. Improve the evaluation and incentive mechanism that conforms to the work rules of juvenile trials.

41. Strengthen coordination and linkage. Strengthen cooperation and coordination with public security organs, procuratorial organs, and judicial administrative organs, establish normalized consultation and collaboration mechanisms, unify standards for evidence and data in cases involving minors, and jointly carry out education, reform, rescue, and judicial assistance work. Strengthen communication and collaboration with government functional departments, the Communist Youth League, the Women's Federation, schools, grassroots organizations, and organizations for the protection of minors, and establish and improve information sharing and notification mechanisms. Promote the improvement of the coordination mechanism for the care, education, and assistance of minors within the political and legal system, and explore the establishment of a pool of personnel for judicial care, education, and assistance of minors, including social workers, volunteers, and "five old personnel" (veteran party members, veterans, veteran teachers, veteran model workers, and veteran cadres).

42. Strengthen guarantees for working conditions. Actively seek leadership from Party committees and support from the government, and ensure that the expenses required for the construction of juvenile trial facilities, the conduct of social investigations, social observation and protection, psychological counseling, legal publicity, family education guidance, and other characteristic trials and extended work are fully included in the scope of case handling expenses, to ensure the effective conduct of juvenile trial work and comprehensively enhance the capacity and level of judicial protection and crime prevention and control for minors.

May 28, 2024
